questions.title: Section A - Multiple Choice, Terminology, Matching, DNA Structure, Meiosis and Dihybrid Inheritance

subQuestions.questionText:
DNA and RNA are examples of …
A) amino acids.
B) enzymes.
C) nucleic acids.
D) proteins.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
DNA and RNA are nucleic acids, the polymers of nucleotides that store and transmit genetic information.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is a product of meiosis?
A) Muscle cell
B) Ovary
C) Nerve cell
D) Ovum
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Meiosis produces gametes (sex cells). An ovum is a gamete, whereas muscle and nerve cells are somatic cells produced by mitosis, and an ovary is an organ.

subQuestions.questionText:
An individual is heterozygous for a harmful recessive allele but is unaffected by it.
Which ONE of the following best represents the genetic composition of this individual?
A) Two dominant normal alleles
B) One harmful recessive allele and one harmful dominant allele
C) One harmful recessive allele and one normal dominant allele
D) One harmful dominant allele and one normal recessive allele
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A heterozygous, unaffected carrier has one harmful recessive allele (not expressed) and one normal dominant allele that masks it.

options.B: One harmful recessive allele and one harmful dominant allele
options.C: One harmful recessive allele and one normal dominant allele
options.D: One harmful dominant allele and one normal recessive allele

subQuestions.questionText:
A person has the genotype I^A i for blood type.
What is this person's blood group?
A) A
B) B
C) O
D) AB
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
I^A is dominant over i, so the genotype I^A i is expressed as blood group A.

subQuestions.questionText:
In a car accident, the biological father of a girl and three other men were killed. The men could not be identified due to their injuries. DNA profiling was used to identify the girl's father. The diagram in the question paper shows the DNA profiles of the girl, her mother and the four men (labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4).
Which ONE of the men is most likely to have been the father of the girl?
A) 4
B) 3
C) 2
D) 1
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Man 3 is the father — the DNA profile bands of the girl that do not match her mother's bands are found in the profile of man 3.

subQuestions.questionText:
A DNA template strand codes for the amino acid serine with any of the following base triplets:
AGA  AGG  AGT  TCA  TCG  AGC
The anticodon that codes for the amino acid serine is …
A) AGT.
B) UGA.
C) TCG.
D) UCG.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The anticodon (on tRNA) is an RNA copy of the DNA template triplet, so T is replaced by U. TCG on the template gives the anticodon UCG.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents two phases of meiosis (phase A and phase B).
Which ONE of the following represents the correct sequence of phases between phase A and phase B?
A) Anaphase I, Metaphase I, Prophase II and Telophase II
B) Metaphase I, Telophase I, Prophase II and Metaphase II
C) Anaphase I, Telophase I, Prophase II, Metaphase II and Anaphase II
D) Prophase I, Telophase I, Prophase II, Metaphase II and Telophase II
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Between the two shown phases the correct order of the intervening phases is Anaphase I, Telophase I, Prophase II, Metaphase II and Anaphase II.

options.A: Anaphase I, Metaphase I, Prophase II and Telophase II
options.B: Metaphase I, Telophase I, Prophase II and Metaphase II
options.C: Anaphase I, Telophase I, Prophase II, Metaphase II and Anaphase II
options.D: Prophase I, Telophase I, Prophase II, Metaphase II and Telophase II

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents a process that occurs during protein synthesis, with parts labelled S, T, U, V and W.
Which ONE of the following is CORRECT?
A) S represents an anticodon
B) W represents mRNA
C) T represents tRNA
D) U represents an amino acid
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Of the statements given, only 'T represents tRNA' correctly matches the labelled part in the diagram.

subQuestions.questionText:
Evidence of hominid cultural evolution can be found in the fossil record.
This evidence would include the …
A) position of the attachment of the spine to the head.
B) length of the upper limbs compared to the length of the lower limbs.
C) number of teeth present in the skull.
D) presence of stone tools.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Stone tools are cultural artefacts and are therefore evidence of hominid cultural evolution. The other options are anatomical (physical), not cultural, evidence.

options.A: position of the attachment of the spine to the head.
options.B: length of the upper limbs compared to the length of the lower limbs.
options.C: number of teeth present in the skull.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: A diagrammatic representation showing possible evolutionary relationships between different species.
subQuestions.memoText: Phylogenetic tree/cladogram (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The type of bond found between amino acids.
subQuestions.memoText: Peptide bond (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The theory that describes evolution as consisting of long periods of little/no change alternating with short periods of rapid change.
subQuestions.memoText: Punctuated equilibrium (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: Similar structures that perform different functions in different organisms.
subQuestions.memoText: Homologous structures (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The breeding of plants and animals by humans for desired characteristics.
subQuestions.memoText: Artificial selection/selective breeding (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The type of dominance where both alleles of a gene are expressed in the phenotype in the heterozygous condition.
subQuestions.memoText: Co-dominance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
COLUMN I: Mechanisms of reproductive isolation
COLUMN II:
A: Species-specific courtship behaviour
B: Breeding at different times of the year
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Both species-specific courtship behaviour and breeding at different times of the year are pre-zygotic reproductive isolation mechanisms.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
COLUMN I: Fossils found in South Africa
COLUMN II:
A: Little Foot
B: Taung Child
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Both Little Foot and the Taung Child are famous hominid fossils discovered in South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B, or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
COLUMN I: Proposed the 'law of use and disuse'
COLUMN II:
A: Eldredge
B: Gould
subQuestions.memoText:
None (2 marks)
The 'law of use and disuse' was proposed by Lamarck. Eldredge and Gould proposed punctuated equilibrium, not this law.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents part of a DNA molecule (Strand 1 and Strand 2), with parts labelled Z, W, X and Y. Identify the:
(a) Molecule X
(b) Sugar at Y
(c) Bond W
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Nitrogenous base/Guanine/Cytosine (1 mark)
(b) Deoxyribose sugar (1 mark)
(c) Hydrogen bond (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the collective name of parts X, Y and Z.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Nucleotide (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the natural shape of the DNA molecule.
subQuestions.memoText: Double helix (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the process whereby DNA makes a copy of itself.
subQuestions.memoText: (DNA) Replication (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO places in an animal cell where DNA is located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (Mark first TWO only):
- Nucleus/Chromosome/Chromatid/Chromatin/Nucleoplasm
- Mitochondria

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents a chromosome pair undergoing a process during meiosis, with area P and structures Q and R labelled. Name the:
(a) Organ in the human male where meiosis occurs
(b) Process represented in the diagram
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Testis (1 mark)
(b) Crossing over (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Label:
(a) Area P
(b) Structure Q
(c) Structure R
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Chiasma (1 mark)
(b) Centromere (1 mark)
(c) Chromatid (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
In humans, short fingers (F) and a widow's peak (H) are dominant over long fingers and continuous hairline. A man and a woman, both heterozygous for the two characteristics, plan on having a child. The table below shows the possible genotypes of the offspring:

Gametes | FH | Fh | fH | fh
FH | FFHH | FFHh | FfHH | FfHh
Fh | FFHh | FFhh | FfHh | Ffhh
fH | FfHH | FfHh | ffHH | Z
fh | FfHh | Ffhh | ffHh | ffhh

State the genotype at Z.
subQuestions.memoText:
ffHh (1 mark)
Z is the offspring of gametes fH (row) and fh (column), giving the genotype ffHh.

subQuestions.questionText:
Using the same dihybrid cross (short fingers F and widow's peak H dominant; both parents heterozygous), give the:
(a) Genotype of the parents
(b) Number of genotypes that could result in offspring with short fingers and a continuous hairline
(c) Allele for a continuous hairline
(d) Phenotype of a child who is homozygous recessive for both characteristics
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) FfHh (2 marks)
(b) 3 (1 mark) [short fingers + continuous hairline = F_hh: FFhh, Ffhh, Ffhh — three genotypes in the table]
(c) h (1 mark)
(d) Long fingers and continuous hairline (2 marks)

questions.title: Section B - Protein Synthesis, Non-disjunction, Karyotypes, Pedigree Analysis and Bone Density

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents two processes (X and Y) that occur during protein synthesis: DNA --(X)--> mRNA --(Y)--> PROTEIN. Where in the cell does EACH of the following processes occur?
(a) X
(b) Y
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) X — Nucleus/nucleoplasm (1 mark)
(b) Y — Ribosome/cytoplasm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE difference between the types of nitrogenous bases found in DNA and RNA.
subQuestions.memoText:
DNA contains thymine/T whereas RNA contains uracil/U (2 marks)
(Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText:
Name and describe process X.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Transcription* (1 compulsory mark) + Any 5 of the following (Total 6 marks):
- The double helix (DNA) molecule unwinds
- The double-stranded DNA unzips/weak hydrogen bonds break
- to form two separate strands
- One strand is used as a template
- to form mRNA
- using free RNA nucleotides from the nucleoplasm
- The mRNA is complementary to the DNA/A-U, G-C
- mRNA now has the coded message for protein synthesis

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how non-disjunction may lead to Down syndrome.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 5):
- When chromosome pair 21/chromosome 21 fails to separate
- during Anaphase
- the daughter cells (gametes) will have 24 chromosomes/an extra chromosome
- When this gamete is fertilised by a normal gamete with 23 chromosomes
- the zygote will have 47 chromosomes/3 chromosomes at position 21/Trisomy 21

subQuestions.questionText: What are somatic cells?
subQuestions.memoText: Body cells/cells in the body except the sex cells (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the chromosomes (karyotypes) from the human somatic cells of two individuals (INDIVIDUAL 1 and INDIVIDUAL 2) who are twins, each showing chromosome pairs numbered 1 to 23. Name the specific type of chromosomes numbered 1 to 22.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Autosomes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Each of the pairs shown is a homologous pair of chromosomes.
(a) State the origin of each chromosome in a homologous pair during zygote formation.
(b) List THREE characteristics that chromosomes in a homologous pair have in common.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) (2 marks)
- One chromosome comes from the sperm/father
- and the other comes from the ovum/mother

(b) Any THREE (Mark first THREE only) (3 marks):
- Shape
- Size/length
- Position of genes/alleles
- Genes coding for same characteristic
- Location of centromere

subQuestions.questionText:
Explain ONE observable reason why the two individuals are not identical twins.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 3):
- Gonosomes are not identical/chromosomes at position 23 are not identical
- Individual 1 has XY gonosomes/is a male
- Individual 2 has XX gonosomes/is a female

subQuestions.questionText:
One type of deafness in humans is carried on a single allele. The pedigree diagram in the question paper shows the inheritance of deafness in a family (individuals John, Mary, Paul, Lizzy, Bob and Ann; KEY: hearing male, deaf male, hearing female, deaf female). How many:
(a) Generations are represented in this pedigree diagram
(b) Children of Paul and Lizzy are able to hear
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) 3/Three (1 mark)
(b) 2/Two (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Which phenotype is dominant?
(Refer to the pedigree diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Hearing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Use the offspring of Bob and Ann to explain your answer to QUESTION 2.4.2.
(Refer to the pedigree diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 4):
- Bob and Ann can both hear
- They have a child who is deaf/who has the genotype aa
- This means that each parent carries an allele for deafness/are heterozygous/Aa
- but it is masked by the dominant allele/which is for hearing

subQuestions.questionText: Use the letter 'A' to represent the dominant allele and the letter 'a' for the recessive allele to give ALL the possible genotypes for a hearing individual.
subQuestions.memoText: AA and Aa (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Use a genetic cross to show how gender in human offspring is determined by the sex chromosomes of the parents.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 'Any 6' marks from the following genetic cross:

P1 Phenotype: Male x Female
Genotype: XY x XX
(Meiosis)
Gametes: X, Y x X, X
(Fertilisation)
F1 Genotype: XX; XX; XY; XY
Phenotype: female : male
(P1 and F1 must be labelled; Meiosis and fertilisation must be shown)

OR (Punnett square layout)
P1 Phenotype: Male x Female
Genotype: XY x XX
(Meiosis)
Gametes:      X        Y
        X   XX       XY
        X   XX       XY
1 mark for correct gametes; 1 mark for correct genotypes
(Fertilisation)
F1 Phenotype: female : male
(P1 and F1; Meiosis and fertilisation)

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the extract: Researchers have discovered that members of a particular family have high bone density that may be caused by a gene mutation. High bone density reduces the risk of bone fractures. Twenty members of the family had their bone density measured and DNA samples taken. Seven had high bone density. The high bone density occurred throughout their bodies but especially in the spine and hips.
From the extract, identify TWO areas in the body where bone density can mainly be measured.
subQuestions.memoText:
- Spine
- Hips
(Mark first TWO only) (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe what a gene mutation is.
subQuestions.memoText:
- A change in the sequence
- of nitrogenous bases/nucleotides in DNA
(2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why it was necessary for the researchers to collect DNA samples.
subQuestions.memoText:
- To check for the gene mutation
- and if it results in the high bone density
(2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the effect of this mutation.
subQuestions.memoText: Produces high bone density/reduces the risk of bone fractures (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage of the family members who had normal bone density. Show ALL your workings.
subQuestions.memoText:
Working (20 family members, 7 with high bone density, therefore 13 with normal bone density):
13/20 x 100 = 65%
OR
7/20 x 100 = 35%; (100 – 35) = 65%

Mark 1: Correct values (13/20 or 7/20)
Mark 2: x 100
Mark 3: 65%
(3 marks)

questions.title: Section B - Cloning, Biogeography, Antibiotic Resistance, Gallfly Investigation and Bipedalism

subQuestions.questionText:
A scientist wanted to clone a straight-haired male horse (horse S) to meet the demand for straight-haired horses. The procedure: the nucleus of a somatic cell was taken from straight-haired male horse S; an unfertilised ovum was removed from curly-haired female horse T; the nucleus from horse S's somatic cell was placed into horse T's ovum; this ovum was then placed into the uterus of female surrogate horse R.
Explain why a somatic cell and NOT a sperm cell from horse S would provide the nucleus for the procedure.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 3):
- The nucleus of the somatic cell is diploid/has a full set of chromosomes/has all the genetic material whereas
- the nucleus of the sperm cell is haploid/contains half the set of chromosomes/has half the genetic material
- The somatic cell carries the desired characteristic/straight hair

subQuestions.questionText:
Before inserting the nucleus from the somatic cell of horse S, the nucleus from the ovum of horse T was removed.
Explain the significance of this procedure.
subQuestions.memoText:
To ensure that (Any TWO, max 2 marks):
- The DNA (of the ovum)/characteristic of curly hair is removed
- Only the desired DNA is present in the clone
- Correct number of chromosomes is present in the clone

subQuestions.questionText: To which of the three horses (S, T or R) will the cloned offspring be genetically identical?
subQuestions.memoText: (Horse) S (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO benefits of cloning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO (Mark first TWO only) (2 marks):
- To produce organisms with desired traits e.g. health, appearance, nutritious, yield, shelf life etc.
- Conservation of threatened species
- To create tissue/organs for transplant

subQuestions.questionText:
The present-day distribution of three closely related species of the dog family — the coyote, jackal and dingo — is shown on the world map in the question paper. What type of evidence for evolution is represented here?
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Biogeography (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: What is a biological species?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 3):
- Similar organisms
- that can interbreed
- to produce fertile offspring

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how these three species (coyote, jackal and dingo) could have evolved from a common ancestor.
subQuestions.memoText:
2 compulsory marks (*) + any 5 (Total 7 marks):
- The original population/common ancestor once lived on a large continent
- and became separated by continental drift/oceans
- There was no gene flow amongst the three populations*
- Each population experienced different environmental conditions
- and underwent natural selection independently
- The individuals in each population became different
- genotypically and phenotypically
- Even if the (three) populations are mixed again
- they would not be able to interbreed/produce fertile offspring
- forming the different species, the coyote, jackal and dingo*

subQuestions.questionText:
Some farmers add low doses of antibiotics to the feed for cattle. The graph in the question paper shows the effect of different doses of antibiotics on the number of harmful bacteria in the cattle (Number of harmful bacteria vs Antibiotic dose in mg). Use evidence from the graph to explain why higher doses of antibiotics will benefit the farmer economically.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 4):
- It decreases the number of harmful bacteria the most
- thereby preventing disease in cattle/resulting in less medical expenses
- Decreasing mortality/maintaining the number of cattle
- to sell/breed/increase profit

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the use of antibiotics in animal feed may result in the evolution of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for any of the following (max 6):
- Natural selection occurs
- There is variation/mutation in the population of bacteria
- Some are resistant to antibiotics, some are non-resistant
- When antibiotic is added to the animal feed
- The bacteria that are non-resistant are killed by the antibiotic
- Those that are resistant survive and reproduce
- The characteristic for resistance to antibiotics is passed on to the offspring
- The next generation will have a higher proportion of antibiotic-resistant bacteria

subQuestions.questionText:
Female gallflies lay eggs on plant stems; the larvae secrete a substance that causes the plant cells to grow into ball-like structures called galls, which are high in nutrients. Predatory birds feed on the larvae in the galls. The size of the galls depends on genetic variation in the gallfly. Scientists investigated whether gall size affects the percentage of gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds. Results:

Gall size (mm) | Gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds (%)
10 | 1
15 | 0
20 | 1
25 | 2
30 | 10

State the:
(a) Independent variable
(b) Dependent variable
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Gall size (1 mark)
(b) Percentage of gallfly larvae killed (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE advantage of the gall to the gallfly larvae.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE (Mark first ONE only) (1 mark):
- Nutrition/food
- Protection
- Space

subQuestions.questionText: State why the size of the galls produced is an example of continuous variation.
subQuestions.memoText: There is a range of (intermediate) values in gall size (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the percentage of gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds is influenced by the size of the gall.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for ONE of the following sets (max 3):

Option 1:
- Larvae in 30 mm galls are eaten more
- since they are more visible to birds and
- contain more/larger larvae

OR

Option 2:
- Larvae in galls that are 25 mm and smaller are eaten less
- since they are less visible to birds and
- contain fewer/smaller larvae

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a line graph to represent the information in the table (Gall size (mm): 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 versus Gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds (%): 1, 0, 1, 2, 10).
subQuestions.memoText:
Guideline for assessing the graph (6 marks):

Correct type of graph (T) — 1 mark: Line graph drawn
Caption of graph (C) — 1 mark: Both variables included (e.g. 'Percentage of gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds due to different gall sizes')
Axes labels (L) — 1 mark: Correct labels and units on X-axis (Gall size (mm)) and Y-axis (Gallfly larvae killed by predatory birds (%))
Scale for X- and Y-axes (S) — 1 mark: Equal spacing between intervals for each axis
Plotting of points (P) — up to 2 marks:
- 1 mark for 1 to 4 points plotted correctly
- 2 marks for all 5 points plotted correctly (10→1, 15→0, 20→1, 25→2, 30→10)

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the pelvic structure (A, B, C) and the ventral view of the skulls (X, Y, Z) of three organisms, drawn to scale. Write down the LETTER(S) of the diagram(s) that represent the:
(a) Skulls of bipedal organisms
(b) Pelvic structure of a quadrupedal organism
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) X, Z (in any order) (2 marks) (Mark first TWO only)
(b) C (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 3.5.1(b).
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for the following (max 2):
- The pelvis is long
- and narrow

subQuestions.questionText: Describe ONE other structural difference between a bipedal and a quadrupedal organism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for ONE of the following sets (Mark first ONE only) (max 3):

Option 1:
- The spine
- is S-shaped for the bipedal organism
- and C-shaped for the quadrupedal organism

OR

Option 2:
- The foramen magnum
- is in a more forward position in bipedal organisms
- and in a backward position in quadrupedal organisms
